experiment_name: Direct win-rate sanity screen: 027's final PURE PPO (hybrid=False) candidate checkpoint vs. its own bit-exact-reconstructed untrained baseline, 20 seeds x 4 focus-seat rotation, deterministic masked-argmax, zero fixed/ASU opponents

algorithm_config.purpose: 027 remains KILL under its own pre-registered proxy rule (ACCEPT_TRADE mean-prior-rank/greedy-rate regressed on a fixed diagnostic set) - but a lower ACCEPT_TRADE rate is not intrinsically evidence of worse play (a rational policy declines bad trades). This screen asks the real question directly: did 32 games of pure PPO training make the checkpoint stronger in actual games, relative to its own starting point? No training, no reward/action-head/factorization changes, no MCTS, no ASU - a pure evaluation.
algorithm_config.design: One CANDIDATE focus seat + three identical copies of the UNTRAINED baseline per game, focus seat rotated across all 4 seats per seed - no scripted fixed agents anywhere, so there is no fixed-agent fallback-substitution path to contaminate results.

baseline.source: 027's own pre-training PPOAgent(hybrid=False) initialization, bit-exact reconstructed (not loaded from a saved file - 027 never saved a pre-training checkpoint) by replaying the identical random.seed(0)/np.random.seed(0)/torch.manual_seed(0) sequence 027's gate script ran immediately before constructing PPOAgent(player_id=0, hybrid=False, device='cpu')
baseline.reproducibility: build_untrained_baseline_agent() re-run independently twice in this experiment's own test suite (tests/test_monopolyzero_pure_ppo_strength_screen.py::test_build_untrained_baseline_agent_is_bit_exact_reproducible) - identical hash both times, matching the pinned value above

algorithm_config.hash_gate: Both actor hashes and the checkpoint file hash were REQUIRED to match 027's own logged values BEFORE any game was played (scripts/monopolyzero_pure_ppo_strength_screen.py::load_candidate_agent / build_untrained_baseline_agent raise SystemExit on any mismatch, refusing to silently retrain/reconstruct) - all three matched on the first attempt, no retry/adjustment needed.
algorithm_config.policy: Deterministic legal-masked argmax over ActorNetwork.forward's log-softmax output for every seat (this project's own build_masked_argmax_policy wrapper, NOT PPOAgent.choose_action, which samples via torch.multinomial - appropriate for training exploration, not evaluation) - zero fixed BUY/TRADE rule, zero MCTS, zero DDQN, zero ASU.
algorithm_config.state_pipeline: monopolyzero_common.ensure_reference_on_path() installs the actor-relative property-owner state-encoding patch (docs/DECISIONS.md's 2026-08-12 entry) globally before any game, active for every seat's env._get_state(seat) call - not just seat 0.
algorithm_config.opponent_pool: 3 copies of the untrained baseline per game - no scripted fixed agents (FPAgentA/B/C), no ASU
algorithm_config.asu_involvement: none - zero ASU imports anywhere in this run's import chain, verified at runtime via monopolyzero_common.loaded_asu_modules() (empty)
algorithm_config.mcts_involvement: none - single deterministic forward pass per decision, no search
algorithm_config.seed_pool: fresh DEV range 46000-46019, registered in scripts/evaluation_protocol.py before this run and validated via evaluation_protocol.require_seed_scope; disjoint from every prior experiment's seeds and from PROMOTION/FINAL_BLIND

pre_registered_decision_rule.primary_statistic: seed-block bootstrap 95% CI (2000 resamples, resampled at the SEED level - the 4 seat-rotation games sharing one seed share a board draw) for (candidate_win_rate - 0.25), via evaluation_protocol.seed_block_bootstrap_vs_null
pre_registered_decision_rule.GO: lower bound of the CI is > 0
pre_registered_decision_rule.KILL: upper bound of the CI is <= 0

result: GO: the seed-block bootstrap 95% CI for (candidate_win_rate - 25% null) is [0.0625, 0.25], entirely above zero (point estimate +16.25 points: candidate won 33/80 = 41.25% vs. the 25% symmetric-skill null, Wilson 95% [31.1%, 52.2%]). 17 of 20 seed blocks had a candidate win rate at or above the null (10 blocks at exactly 2/4=50%, 2 blocks at 3/4=75%), only 3 blocks had zero candidate wins - the signal is broad across seeds, not one outlier block. Candidate also carried a +2021.9 mean net-worth advantage and a lower bankruptcy rate (23.75% vs. 54.17%) than the untrained baseline. The dominant behavioral driver is BUY_PROPERTY: candidate bought 98.5% of legal opportunities vs. baseline's 0.59% - consistent with 027's own diagnostic finding that BUY_PROPERTY became strongly learnable. ACCEPT_TRADE did move in the direction 027 flagged (candidate 71.4% vs. baseline 74.9% accept-when-legal, i.e. candidate accepts trades slightly less often) but this did not cost the candidate real strength; per this task's framing, a lower accept rate is not intrinsically bad play (a rational policy should decline bad trades), and the real-game outcome confirms it did not hurt win rate here. Zero illegal actions, zero crashes, zero fixed-agent fallbacks (no scripted agents in this design), zero ASU modules loaded across all 80 games. This answers the specific question this screen was built for - the 32-game pure PPO update did create real, statistically supported game strength relative to its own initialization - it does not reverse 027's own KILL verdict under 027's different, pre-registered proxy rule (mean prior rank/greedy-choice rate on a fixed diagnostic set), and it is not a claim of strength against fixed agents, ASU, or any other opponent family - only against this checkpoint's own untrained starting point.
notes: Checkpoint and reconstructed-baseline weights are not committed per CLAUDE.md - referenced by SHA-256 and local path only. round_cap_rate (85%, 68/80) is notably higher than prior paired evals in this project (e.g. 013/014's 45-55%) - plausibly because neither side here ever chooses DECLINE_TRADE (0% rate when legal for both candidate and baseline, seen already in a smaller 4-game dry run before this experiment) and both sides trade very actively (287-330 trade offers/game), which may extend games rather than driving faster bankruptcies; not investigated further here; this evaluation did not run against fixed agents or ASU, and no claim is made about strength against those opponent families. accept_trade/decline_trade opportunity counts are identical by construction (ACCEPT_TRADE and DECLINE_TRADE are always legal together whenever a trade response decision exists).
